paragraphs: As used herein, the "Company," "Rogers," "we," "us," "our" and similar terms include Rogers Corporation and its subsidiaries, unless the context indicates otherwise.

This Annual Report on Form 10-K includes "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Exchange Act. Such statements are generally accompanied by words such as "anticipate," "assume," "believe," "could," "estimate," "expect," "foresee," "goal," "intend," "may," "might," "plan," "potential," "predict," "project," "should," "seek," "target" or similar expressions that convey uncertainty as to future events or outcomes. Forward-looking statements are based on assumptions and beliefs that we believe to be reasonable; however, assumed facts almost always vary from actual results, and the differences between assumed facts and actual results could be material depending upon the circumstances. Where we express an expectation or belief as to future results, that expectation or belief is expressed in good faith and based on assumptions believed to have a reasonable basis. We cannot assure you, however, that the stated expectation or belief will occur or be achieved or accomplished. Among the factors that could cause our results to differ materially from those indicated by forward-looking statements are risks and uncertainties inherent in our business including, without limitation:
•failure to capitalize on, volatility within, or other adverse changes with respect to growth opportunities, such as delays in adoption or implementation of new technologies;

•uncertain business, economic and political conditions in the U.S. and abroad, particularly in China, Germany, England, Belgium, South Korea and Hungary where we maintain significant manufacturing, sales or administrative operations;

•the global trade policy dynamics between nations reflected in trade agreement negotiations, the imposition of tariffs and other trade restrictions, as well as the potential for global supply chain decoupling;
•fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates;
•our ability to develop innovative products and the extent to which they are incorporated into end-user products and systems that achieve commercial success;
•the ability and willingness of our sole or limited source suppliers to deliver certain key raw materials, including commodities, to us in a timely and cost-effective manner;
•business interruptions due to catastrophes or other similar events, such as natural disasters, war, terrorism or public health crises;
•the impact of sanctions, export controls and other foreign asset or investment restriction;

•failure to realize, or delays in the realization of, anticipated benefits of acquisitions and divestitures due to, among other things, the existence of unknown liabilities or difficulty integrating acquired businesses;
•our ability to attract and retain management and skilled technical personnel;
•our ability to protect our proprietary technology from infringement by third parties and/or allegations that our technology infringes third party rights;
•changes in effective tax rates or tax laws and regulations in the jurisdictions in which we operate;

headings: Risks Relating to Our Business, Strategy and Operations
Failure to capitalize on, volatility within, or other adverse changes with respect to the Company's growth opportunities may adversely affect our business.
We face intense global competition, which could reduce demand for our products or create additional pricing pressure on our products.
Our business is dependent upon our development of innovative products and our customers' incorporation of those products into end user products and systems that achieve commercial success.
Macroeconomic conditions could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, or results of operations.
Our dependence on sole or limited source suppliers for certain of our raw materials could materially adversely affect our ability to manufacture products and materially increase our costs.
Our business strategy includes plans for organic growth, and our results of operations and financial position could be adversely affected if we fail to grow or fail to manage our growth effectively.
We rely on highly specialized technical personnel and management, and the failure to attract and retain these individuals could impair our expected growth and future success.
If we suffer loss or disruption to our facilities, supply chains, distribution systems or information technology systems due to catastrophe or other events, our business could be seriously harmed.

We have extensive international operations, and events and circumstances that have general international consequence or specific impact in the countries in which we operate may materially adversely affect our business.
A significant disruption in, or breach in security of, our information technology systems or violations of data protection laws could materially adversely affect our business and reputation.
Emerging issues related to the development and use of AI could give rise to legal or regulatory action, damage our reputation, or otherwise materially harm our business.
We may experience difficulties in implementing our new ERP system.
We are subject to many environmental laws and regulations as well as potential environmental liabilities that could adversely affect our business.
Our business may be materially adversely affected if we cannot protect our proprietary technology or if we infringe the proprietary rights of others.

As a multinational corporation doing business in the U.S. and various foreign jurisdictions, changes in tax laws or exposures to additional tax liability could negatively impact our operating results.
The terms of our credit agreement subject us to risks if we fail to satisfy financial ratios and comply with numerous covenants.
We may be adversely affected by litigation stemming from product liability and other claims.
We may incur substantial costs to comply with climate change legislation and related regulatory initiatives.
Our business could be negatively affected as a result of actions of activist shareholders, and such activism could impact the trading value of our securities.
paragraphs: Our business, results of operations and financial position are subject to various risks, including those discussed below, which may affect the value of our capital stock. The following risk factors, which we believe represent the most significant factors that may make an investment in our capital stock risky, may cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected in any forward-looking statement. You should carefully consider these factors, as well as the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the information set forth in "Item 1. Business - Forward-Looking Statements" and "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Results of Operations and Financial Position," when evaluating an investment in our capital stock.

We continue to target growth opportunities in the EV/HEV, ADAS, portable electronics, renewable energy, aerospace and defense and other markets. These growth opportunities, as well as specific market and industry trends within them, may be volatile, cyclical and sensitive to a variety of factors, including general economic conditions (including higher inflation and interest rates), demand disruptions (including third-party component availability at our customers), technology disruptions, consumer preferences and political priorities. Adverse or cyclical changes to and within these growth opportunities, such as delays in adoption or implementation of new technologies, have resulted in, and may continue to result in, reduced demand for certain of our products, production overcapacity, increased inventory levels and related risks of obsolescence, as well as price erosion, ultimately leading to a decline in our operating results. Acceleration within these growth opportunities and corresponding rapid increases in demand for certain products may also require us to make significant capital investments or acquisitions in facilities and information systems and significantly increase our personnel in order to increase production levels and to maintain customer relationships and market positions. However, we may not be able to increase our production levels with sufficient speed or efficiency to capitalize on such increases in demand.
We operate in a highly competitive global environment and compete with domestic and international companies principally on the basis of the following:
•innovation; •historical customer relationships; •product quality, reliability, performance and price;
•technical and engineering service and support; •breadth of product line; and

Our competitors include commodity materials suppliers, which offer product substitutions based mostly on price, and suppliers of alternate solutions, which offer product substitutions or eliminations based mostly on disruptive technology. Certain of these competitors have greater financial and other resources than we have, and, in some cases, these competitors are well established in specific product niches. We expect that our competitors will continue to improve the design and performance of their products, which could result in the development of products that offer price or performance features superior to our products. Furthermore, our customers may engage in internal manufacturing of products that may result in reduced demand for our products. If we are unable to maintain our competitive advantage for any reason, demand for our products may be materially reduced, which may adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial position.

paragraphs: The following key highlights and factors should be considered when reviewing our results of operations, financial position and liquidity:

•In 2025, as compared to 2024, our net sales decreased by 2.3% to $810.8 million, our gross margin decreased 170 basis points to 31.7% from 33.4%, and operating income as a percentage of net sales decreased 860 basis points to (5.6%) from 3.0%.

•We recognized impairment charges of $71.8 million in 2025 related to our curamik® reporting unit within our AES operating segment, and $1.9 million related to the impairment of our facility lease in Mexico.

•We recognized restructuring charges of $23.4 million in 2025 due to our wind down of manufacturing operations for our AES operating segment in our Evergem, Belgium facility, phase one of curamik® manufacturing footprint consolidation, our executive leadership transition, and the reduction of our global workforce.
•We repurchased 738,145 shares of our capital stock for $52.4 million in 2025.

paragraphs: 審閱我們營運成果、財務狀況及流動性時，應考量以下關鍵重點及因素：
•2025 年，與 2024 年相比，我們的淨銷售額減少 2.3% 至 810.8 百萬美元，毛利率減少 170 基點至 31.7%（由 33.4% 下降），營運收入佔淨銷售額百分比減少 860 基點至 (5.6%)（由 3.0% 下降）。
•我們在 2025 年認列與 curamik® 報告單位相關的減損費用 71.8 百萬美元，該單位屬於我們 AES 營運分部；以及與墨西哥廠房租賃減損相關的費用 1.9 百萬美元。
•我們在 2025 年認列 23.4 百萬美元的重整費用，原因包括我們 AES 營運分部在 Evergem, Belgium 廠區關閉製造業務、curamik® 製造據點整合第一階段、高階管理層變動，以及全球員工數量減少。
•我們在 2025 年以 52.4 百萬美元購回 738,145 股本公司資本股票。

headings: 與本公司業務、策略及營運相關之風險
未能把握、營運波動或其它不利變動，可能對本公司之業務造成不利影響。
我們面臨激烈之全球性競爭，這可能會降低我們產品之需求，或對我們產品造成額外之價格壓力。
我們之業務依賴於創新產品之開發，以及客戶將這些產品整合至終端用戶產品與系統中，以實現商業成功。
總體經濟條件可能對我們之業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。
我們對某些原材料依賴單一或有限來源供應商，這可能會對我們製造產品之能力造成重大不利影響，並大幅提高我們之成本。
我們之業務策略包含計畫進行內生性成長，若我們未能成長或未能有效管理成長，可能會對我們之營運成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
我們依賴高度專業之技術人員與管理階層，若無法吸引並留住這些人才，可能會影響我們預期之成長與未來成功。
若我們因災難或其他事件導致廠區、供應鏈、配送系統或資訊科技系統遭受損失或中斷，將可能嚴重影響本公司業務。
本公司擁有廣泛的國際營運，若發生具有一般國際影響或對我們營運國家有特定衝擊的事件與情勢，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
若資訊科技系統發生重大中斷或安全事件，或違反資料保護法規，可能對本公司業務與聲譽造成重大不利影響。
與人工智慧（AI）發展與應用相關的新興議題，可能引發法律或監管行動，損害本公司聲譽，或以其他方式對本公司業務造成重大損害。
本公司可能面臨在實施新 ERP 系統時遇到困難。
本公司受許多環境法規與潛在環境責任所影響，這些因素可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
若本公司無法保護其專屬技術或侵犯他人的專屬權利，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
作為一家在美國及多個外國司法管轄區域營運的跨國企業，稅法變更或面臨額外稅務負擔可能對我們的營運成果產生負面影響。
我們信貸協議的條款使我們面臨若未能符合財務比率及遵守多項契約義務的風險。
我們可能因產品責任及其他聲請而面臨不利影響。
我們可能因符合氣候變遷立法及相關監管措施而產生重大成本。
我們的業務可能因激進股東的行動而受到負面影響，且此種 activism 可能影響我們證券的交易價值。
paragraphs: 本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況受多種風險影響，包括下文所述之風險，這些風險可能影響本公司資本股票之價值。以下風險因素，本公司認為是可能使投資本公司資本股票風險最高的因素，可能導致本公司實際結果與任何財務預測聲明有重大差異。您在評估投資本公司資本股票時，應謹慎考慮這些因素，以及本年度10-K表報表中所包含的其他資訊，包括「項目1.業務-前瞻性陳述」及「項目7.管理層對營運成果及財務狀況之討論與分析」所載資訊。

本公司持續尋求在電動車/混合動力車、ADAS、便攜式電子產品、可再生能源、航空與防禦及其他市場的成長機會。這些成長機會，以及其內部特定市場與產業趨勢，可能具有波動性、週期性，且對多種因素敏感，包括總體經濟狀況（包括通貨膨脹與利率提高）、需求中斷（包括客戶端零組件供應不足）、技術中斷、消費者偏好與政治優先事項。這些成長機會的不利或週期性變化，例如新技術採用或實施的延遲，已導致，且可能繼續導致，某些產品需求減少、產能過度、存貨水準增加及相關過時風險，以及價格下滑，最終導致本公司營運成果下降。這些成長機會的加速，以及對某些產品需求的快速增加，也可能要求本公司進行重大資本投資或收購廠房與資訊系統，並大幅增加人力，以提高生產水準，並維持客戶關係與市場地位。然而，本公司可能無法以足夠的速度或效率提高生產水準，以把握這些需求增加的機會。
本公司營運於高度競爭的全球環境中，與國內外公司主要競爭因素如下：
•創新；•歷史客戶關係；•產品品質、可靠性、性能與價格；
•技術與工程服務及支援；•產品線廣度；以及

本公司競爭對手包括提供替代解決方案的廠商，這些廠商主要根據價格提供產品替代方案，以及提供替代解決方案的廠商，這些廠商主要根據顛覆性技術提供產品替代方案或淘汰。其中一些競爭對手擁有比本公司更優越的財務及其他資源，在某些情況下，這些競爭對手在特定產品細分市場已建立穩固地位。本公司預期這些競爭對手將持續改進其產品設計與性能，這可能會導致開發出具備較佳價格或性能特徵的產品，優於本公司產品。此外，本公司客戶可能進行內部製造，這可能會導致本公司產品需求減少。若本公司無法因任何原因維持競爭優勢，本公司產品需求可能大幅減少，這可能會對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
